# Pagecairn v0.1.0

The first public release of Pagecairn: a lightweight, self-hosted wiki for small software teams.

> **Historical release:** this tag predates completion of the Pagecairn naming
> update. New installations should use v0.1.1 or newer for consistently named
> application source and Docker Compose resources.

## Highlights

- Create, edit, nest, move, search, and restore documentation pages.
- Write rich text, code, tables, checklists, links, images, and file attachments.
- Invite teammates with local Admin and Member accounts; no email provider required.
- Keep the complete installation in one persistent `/data` volume using SQLite and local uploads.
- Run the application as one Docker container with no required external services.

## Install

This release is distributed as source and built locally with Docker:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bybogdan/pagecairn.git
cd pagecairn
git checkout v0.1.0
docker compose up -d --build
```

Open `http://localhost:3000` for local evaluation. Read the
[self-hosting guide](https://github.com/bybogdan/pagecairn/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) before exposing a production
installation: port 3000 is plain HTTP and production deployments require TLS
through a reverse proxy with secure session cookies enabled.

## Data and updates

All persistent state is stored in `/data`, including `database.sqlite`, its
WAL/SHM files when present, and `uploads/`. Back up the complete data directory
before updating. Do not copy only the SQLite file and do not run
`docker compose down -v` unless you intend to delete the installation data.

Follow the documented tagged update, health-check, log-review, and recovery
procedure in the [self-hosting guide](https://github.com/bybogdan/pagecairn/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md).

## Known limitations

- One workspace per installation.
- Local email/password authentication; no external identity providers.
- Invitation links must be shared manually; no email delivery service is included.
- Local filesystem uploads and SQLite are the supported default storage model.
- No real-time multiplayer editing.
- No prebuilt container image is published for this release; build from the tagged source.

These limits are intentional for the initial focused, self-hosted release.
